lines: GOLDSKIN MINING Co. SURFACE WATER. The NORTH RUN and JUNCTION 3 off the SUMP. The GANGERS' CHAMBER, the VALVE HOUSE, the EAST RUN and the WEST RUN off JUNCTION 3, each run behind a penstock. The OUTFALL through the WEST RUN, on a Company padlock; the OUTFALL's ladder comes up in the Works yard, inside the wall.

The EAST VALVE decides which penstock is up. Ladders up to the street from the NORTH RUN, the EAST RUN and the WEST RUN. The doors off the SUMP and off JUNCTION 3 have their names stencilled beside them.
Covers are not to be lifted from the street. They lift from below, and that is the way they were meant to lift.
JUNCTION 3. DEPTH FOUR METRES. Do not stand in the east run while the valve is being turned.
Under it, in chalk: we stand in it. The water is slow for the first nine seconds and then it is not.
EAST VALVE. One side runs and one side is dry. There is no setting in which both are dry.
Turned by the ganger on shift, at six and at six. The log has been kept up every day since the shift stopped.
A dry chamber off the junction. The brazier is banked and there is a kettle beside it that is still warm.
Nothing walks in here. The door was wedged from this side, and whoever wedged it did it neatly.
SUMP. The grate up to Castle.
NORTH RUN. Ladder up to the town.
Under it, in chalk: rungs out. Iron in the ganger's box.
GANGERS' CHAMBER. Dry. The brazier is kept in.
VALVE HOUSE. The EAST VALVE. Turned at six and at six.
EAST RUN. The penstock is up while the east is dry.
WEST RUN. To the OUTFALL. The penstock is up while the east runs.
